title: SE Enablement: Messaging & Competitive Demo Practice
summary: Internal SE/AE enablement session focused on sharpening messaging, handling competitor objections, and running demo practice with callouts for Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private positioning.
topics: Demo script: latency/cost tradeoffs, KV cache, autoscaling, rollouts
Next steps: updated cheat sheet, practice runs, recording share
transcript:
[00:00:00] Alex: Okay team, we'll kick off at 3:00pm. Thanks for joining, quick agenda: messaging refresh, competitor callouts, then two demo runs. Everyone good?
[00:00:18] Priya: Yep, ready. I sent the slide deck earlier, page 4 has the updated value props.
[00:00:25] Jordan: Great, first up — the one-liner. We keep saying 'developer-first inference platform for production economics'—let's make that sharper for customers.
[00:00:40] Alex: Proposed: 'Make high-performance, reliable LLM inference predictable and economical across any deployment.' Short and hits the thesis.
[00:00:52] Maya: Callout: sales decks need the throughput/latency numbers on page 6, customers always ask for that.
[00:01:05] Priya: When customers say "why not OpenAI", we should lead with routing flexibility and Dedicated capacity: predictable throughput and data isolation.
[00:01:22] Jordan: Also emphasize cost levers: batching, KV caching, quantization profiles — that's our angle vs managed endpoints that are opaque on unit economics.
[00:01:35] Alex: Good. Let's role-play: I'll be a prospect worried about latency/cost. Priya, defend Dedicated vs Hosted.
[00:01:50] Priya: Sure — so if latency under 200ms P95 is a hard requirement, Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools and config to hit that; we also support private deployment if you need VPC/prem. Hosted is faster to spin up and great for less-sensitive workloads.
[00:02:10] Alex: Prospect: "Dedicated is expensive" — what do you say?
[00:02:18] Priya: We run the math — usually, committed capacity plus batching and KV cache drops your per-token by 40-60% for steady workloads. We have cost models and Optimize suggestions we can share.
[00:02:30] Jordan: Add concrete example: a 2M tokens/day ecommerce workflow moved from hosted to dedicated and saw per-token cost cut by ~50% while improving stability.
[00:02:45] Maya: Note to slide update: add that customer example anonymized.
[00:02:52] Alex: Competitors — let's list them. Who's at the top of the list?
[00:03:00] Priya: OpenAI for easy dev UX and large model access; Anthropic for safety and instruction-tuning claims; Hugging Face for model catalog and community, Replicate/Spell for edge use cases; proprietary infra vendors that sell hardware + runtime.
[00:03:20] Jordan: For each competitor, we need a one-liner rebuttal. OpenAI: best for quick start but limited options for private deployments and fine-grained routing or committed SLAs. Anthropic: strong safety messaging, but fewer deployment modes. Hugging Face: great for openness but customers still need infra to get production SLAs.
[00:03:42] Priya: Also call out that some customers will bring up LlamaIndex/Weaviate when we discuss retrieval — position: we integrate with common retrieval layers, and our Optimize tooling helps tune cache and embedding strategies.
[00:03:58] Alex: Ok, demo practice — run 1, Priya will walk through a hosted-to-dedicated migration scenario, highlight config changes and tracing in Console.
[00:04:15] Priya: Starting share — opening Console, route map -> showing model catalog, we have Redwood-verified perf profiles. Notice the P95/throughput badges.
[00:04:40] [00:04:40] Alex: (whisper) Watch the timing, call out the KV cache example when you hit the sample.
[00:04:50] Priya: Right — demo script: start with simple generation, then show prefix caching reducing repeated context cost, then show canary rollout to Dedicated.
[00:05:06] Priya: Demo: baseline hosted call, latency ~220ms on small prompt, then enable prefix caching — repeated prompts drop to 80ms.
[00:05:22] Alex: Customer low-latency rebuttal: "We need <100ms from EU to EU" — how do you respond?
[00:05:30] Priya: We offer region pinning and Dedicated in EU regions; with proper batching and cache warmup, hitting <100ms for typical prompt lengths is possible. We can run a benchmark on your workload as a POC.
[00:05:46] Jordan: Important to mention fallback policies: if Dedicated can't handle a spike we can route to hosted with controls so service remains available.
[00:06:00] Priya: Next up: security slide — SSO, SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS integrations.
[00:06:12] Alex: Prospect will ask about SOC 2 and data retention. Standard line: SOC 2 Type II in progress / available (pick current status), audit logs in Console, customer-managed KMS available for Private.
[00:06:30] Priya: Also mention Private on-prem option for regulated workloads, plus VPC peering for cloud private deployments.
[00:06:45] Maya: Note: update the security appendix with the KMS flow diagram.
[00:06:52] [00:07:00] Alex: Let's run a harder role-play — customer compares us to Anthropic and says Anthropic is safer for instruction-tuned tasks.
[00:07:10] Priya: Acknowledge safety claims, then pivot: our evaluation suite ties regressions to prompt sets and we have quality monitoring + regression alerts; plus you can choose model variants and control rollouts. Safety is a multilayer problem — model selection, evals, and runtime controls.
[00:07:34] Jordan: Use the evals example — during onboarding we ran prompt-set regression detection and prevented a rollout that caused hallucinations on e-commerce SKU sentences.
[00:07:50] Alex: Good. Now a live demo practice — Priya will intentionally trip the fallback to show tracing and incident analysis.
[00:08:05] Priya: Triggering a canary that exceeds capacity — Console shows automatic fallback to hosted, trace shows request path, error rate panel spikes, and rollbacks can be automated.
[00:08:25] Alex: Prospects love seeing the rollback in action. Make sure to point out SLO dashboard and token-level cost.
[00:08:40] [00:09:00] Maya: Quick objection library refresher — price, latency, compliance, vendor lock-in. We have stock responses on the shared drive.
[00:09:12] Priya: On vendor lock-in, emphasize standard APIs and model catalog — customers can pin model versions and route to compatible variants. Also our SDKs are lightweight.
[00:09:28] Jordan: Practice two-minute pitch now. Alex, you time.
[00:09:35] Alex: Go.
[00:09:36] Priya: Redwood Inference gives you a predictable, economical way to run LLMs in production across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Our runtime optimizes for throughput and latency with batching, KV caching, and quantization-friendly execution; our Console provides per-route cost and latency visibility and rollout controls for safe deployments. For customers with strict latency or compliance needs, Dedicated and Private options plus KMS and audit logs provide the necessary isolation and controls.
[00:10:10] Alex: Nice. Clean. A couple of edits: shorten "quantization-friendly execution" to "quantization support" and call out "canary and automatic rollback" in the last line.
[00:10:24] Priya: Noted.
[00:10:30] [00:10:40] Alex: Now mock pricing question — customer: "what's the ballpark for 100M tokens/month?"
[00:10:48] Jordan: We don't give sticker price live, ask about model mix and latency SLOs then run the cost calculator; offer a pilot to collect telemetry.
[00:11:00] Priya: If pushed, give a range and say dedicated with a commit usually saves money at that volume. Provide the cost model spreadsheet post-call.
[00:11:12] Maya: Action: attach cost model template to the enablement follow-up.
[00:11:20] [00:11:30] Alex: Let's practice a security deep-dive Q: "How do you ensure customer data isn't logged in hosted?"
[00:11:40] Priya: By default we retain logs for X days for diagnostics (update placeholder), customers can opt-out or choose Private where data never leaves their VPC; also support customer-managed KMS to prevent us from decrypting stored artifacts.
[00:12:02] Jordan: Flag — make sure the docs include the data retention defaults.
[00:12:10] Alex: Demo run two — shorter, focus on competitive differentiators and rebuttals. Priya, start.
[00:12:20] Priya: Short pitch and then show Console > Optimize suggestions -> quantization recommendation for a transformer-70b style model showing latency/cost tradeoff.
[00:12:45] Alex: Callout when you toggle quantization settings — say expected accuracy delta and validation steps.
[00:12:53] Priya: Right, say: "We recommend quantization for throughput-sensitive workloads; we surface expected quality delta and run evals against your prompt set."
[00:13:08] Maya: Reminder: include the 'quality monitoring and regression alerts' line in the one-pager.
[00:13:18] [00:13:30] Alex: We had a thread earlier about community open models — what if a customer wants full open-source stack and we're asked about HF?
[00:13:40] Priya: Say: Hugging Face is great; Redwood complements that by offering a production runtime and SLAs — you can still bring HF models into our catalog.
[00:13:52] Jordan: Competitive nugget: for customers focused on research and experimentation, HF + self-host is fine; for product teams shipping customers will care about SLOs and cost predictability.
[00:14:06] Alex: Time check — 45 minutes left. We're on track. Next, finalize the cheat-sheet edits and run two more micro-practices next week.
[00:14:18] Priya: Micro-practice sign-up: I'll take the first slot, Jordan second, Alex third.
[00:14:26] Maya: I'll circulate the updated deck and the objection cheat sheet after notes updates.
[00:14:34] [00:14:40] Alex: Quick lightning round — one-liners for each competitor.
[00:14:45] Priya: OpenAI: easiest to start, limited enterprise controls. Anthropic: strong safety posture, fewer deployment options. Hugging Face: community and model catalog, less turnkey infra. Replicate: great for edge/hosting images, not full enterprise-grade runtime.
[00:15:10] Jordan: Nice. Okay demo practice wrap, final role-play where I play a tough procurement leader.
[00:15:20] Alex: Jump in.
[00:15:22] Jordan: Procurement: "We need IP indemnity and strict data residency — can you do EU-only data flow and contract terms?"
[00:15:32] Priya: Yes, we offer region pinning and private deployments; legal can do enterprise addenda for indemnity clauses — we'll route to sales legal early.
[00:15:44] Alex: Mention that Dedicated contracts have SLA clauses and enterprise support tiers.
[00:15:50] Maya: Action: add a prompt for AE to request legal templates when procurement shows up.
[00:15:58] [00:16:10] Alex: Ok time for final recap & next steps.
[00:16:15] Priya: Recap: update deck with anonymous customer example, security appendix with KMS flow, attach cost model spreadsheet, update objection cheat sheet, schedule three micro-practice sessions.
[00:16:30] Alex: Great. Who owns each?
[00:16:34] Maya: I'll own deck updates and distribution.
[00:16:38] Priya: I'll take the objection cheat sheet and lead micro-practices.
[00:16:42] Jordan: I'll coordinate the demo recording and practice schedule.
[00:16:47] Alex: I'll follow up with the cost model and the security doc links.
[00:16:52] Maya: Ok I'll send calendar invites for micro-practice next week.
[00:16:58] Alex: Anything else?
[00:17:02] Priya: Nothing from me.
[00:17:05] Jordan: All good.
[00:17:10] Alex: Thanks everyone, end.
